 It’s time to get out your water guns. An iconic music festival hailing from Korea will make its debut in Toronto next year.
 Waterbomb, known for combining K-pop, EDM and hip-hop performances with interactive water gunfights and giant water cannons, will touch down in the city in 2027.
 “Toronto, it’s time to get wet,” organizers said. “Experience a revolutionizing paradigm of music festival where you get to become a player and a creator of the entire experience: entertainment, performances, and water-battle.”
 ARTICLE CONTINUES BELOW 
 View this post on Instagram 
 A post shared by WATERBOMB TORONTO (@waterbomb_toronto_official) 
 While a date and lineup for the Toronto celebration has yet to be unveiled, the festival has previously welcomed artists including Jay Park, Lee Young Ji, Jessi and 2NE1 to stages in Seoul, Incheon, Busan and beyond.
 ARTICLE CONTINUES BELOW 
 The festival has also taken place in Bali, Singapore, Manila and more.
 “The official performance schedule and set times will be released closer to the festival,” organizers said, urging guests to keep a lookout online for updates.
 ARTICLE CONTINUES BELOW 
 Aside from the live performances, guests in Toronto can also look forward to creative art and pop-up spaces, trendy K-food and a VIP lounge at the festival. Plus, fans will be able to bring their own water guns.
 ARTICLE CONTINUES BELOW
 While a venue for Toronto’s Waterbomb bash is still under wraps, popular outdoor concert and music festival settings in the city include Rogers Stadium, along with Downsview Park.
 As we wait for more to be revealed, those interested in attending Waterbomb in Toronto can sign up online to the super early bird sale.
 More K-pop concerts in Toronto
 Aside from Waterbomb, Toronto has seen a wave of K-pop acts perform in the city as of late.
 Globally-recognized K-pop girl group BLACKPINK took the stage at Toronto’s Rogers Stadium in the summer of 2025, while K-pop royalty BTS performed at the venue this August.
 Next year, Stray Kids will bring their Run It tour to Rogers Stadium on June 25. Tickets go on sale to the public on Nov. 19 on Ticketmaster.
